body.p: Claims 21, 23-26, 29, 31-37, and 39-50 are pending. Claims 1-20, 22, 27, 28, 30, and 38 are cancelled. Claim 21 is amended without prejudice to, or disclaimer of, the underlying subject matter. Support for the amendments may be found in the original claims and specification, e.g., at paragraph [0062] and Example 1. No new matter enters by way of the present amendments. Reconsideration of the application based on the above amendments and following remarks is respectfully requested.
A. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and further in
view of Bennett-Guerrero
The Examiner rejects claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly

being unpatentable over US Publication 2016/0338591 to Lachenbruch et al. ("Lachenbruch") in view of US Publication 2015/0186607 to Geleijnse et al. ("Geleijnse"), further in view of "Capacitive Biosensors" (Berggren et al., Electroanalysis, 13(3):173-180 (2001)) ("Berggren"), and further in view of US Patent 9,028,407 to Bennett-Guerrero ("Bennett-Guerrero"). See Office Action at pp. 7-8.

Specifically, the Examiner asserts that "Lachenbruch et al. teaches... do nothing if the delta value does not exceed the threshold... ." Office Action at page 8. The Examiner acknowledges that "while Lachenbruch et al. does disclose SEM measurements and calculating if a threshold is exceeded fUro]m measured patient values, it does not explicitly teach a current intervention as well as the optionality to change the intervention based on the measurements." Office Action at pages 9-10. Applicant thanks the Examiner for acknowledging that "Lachenbruch et al. may not further, specifically teach... making a further plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K... continuing to administer the current PU intervention, and ... calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of measurements." Office Action at page 10 (emphasis added).

The Examiner further alleges that "Geleinjse et al. teaches... continuing to administer the current PU intervention... ." Office Action at page 11. The Examiner alleges that "Berggren teaches... calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of measurements...." Office Action at page 11. The Examiner also alleges that "Bennett-Guerrero teaches...making the further plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K...making the further plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N...where N has a value greater than K...." Office Action at page 11.

Lastly, the Examiner alleges that combining Bennet-Guerrero with "the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., and Berggren in combination with the motivation(s) of being beneficial for various reasons such as to enhance, improve, or even optimize battery life." Office Action at page 13. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Applicant respectfully submits that aprimafacie case of obviousness has not been established for amended claim 21 for at least the following two reasons: (a) Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21 and (b) a person of ordinary skill in the art combining the cited references would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter with a reasonable expectation of success.
(a) Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett-Guerrero, alone or in
combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21
Applicant respectfully submits that Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett- Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21.
It is well-established law for an obviousness rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 that the
references, either alone or combined, must provide all of the elements of the claim. The Office is required to make "a searching comparison of the claimed invention - including all its limitations

- with the teaching of the prior art." In re Ochiai, 71 F.3d 1565, 1572 (Fed. Cir. 1995), and CFMT v. Yieldup Intern. Corp., 349 F.3d 1333, 1342 (Fed. Cir. 2003). When "[t]he prior art reference (or references when combined) [do] not teach or suggest all the claimSVG {EMBED HERE} 0.1430.99 [o]ffice personnel must explain why the difference(s) between the prior art andthe claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art." M.P.E.P. at § 2141 (III).

The Examiner has not at least shown that the cited references, alone or in combination, provide or suggest "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements", let alone "making a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, wherein the pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K is longer than every 15 minutes." as is recited in amended claim 21.

The Examiner acknowledges that Lachenbruch "may not further, specifically teach:... do something by continuing to administer the current PU intervention and making a plurality of measurement at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K... and... calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements... ." Office Action at page 10.

Geleijnse does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch. The Examiner alleges that Geleijnse teaches "do nothing by continuing to administer the current PU intervention." Office Action at page 11. At best, Geliejnse recites "decisions support... to assist the clinician to make educated decisions on the transition of the patient to a different level of care (or to better stay in the current level of care)." However, Geleijnse is silent as to "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements", let alone "making a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, wherein the pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K is longer than every 15 minutes." as is recited in amended claim 21.

Berggren does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch and Geleijnse. The Examiner alleges Berggren teaches "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of measurements." Office Action at page 11. Applicant respectfully disagrees. At best, Berggren recites "Capacitive affinity biosensors can be constructed by immobilizing recognition elements in thin layers on an electrode or between two electrodes and measuring changes in the dielectric properties when an analyte binds." Berggren at 3rd paragraph of Introduction (emphasis added). Applicant respectfully submits that Berggren is completely silent as to "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements", let alone "making a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, wherein the pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K is longer than every 15 minutes." as is recited in amended claim 21.
Bennet-Guerrero does not remedy the deficiencies of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse and

Berggren. The Examiner alleges that "one of ordinary skill...would have found it obvious to 2a) make a further plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level- K and 2b) make the further plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N, where N has a value greater than K as taught by Bennet- Guerrero in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., and Berggren in combination with the motivation(s) of being beneficial for various reasons such as to enhance, improve, or even optimize battery life." Office Action at page 13. Applicant disagrees. At best, Bennett- Guerrero recites that when a "patient's heart rate and respiratory rates slow, such as 10% lower than the median value obtained during day time, and the patient is subject to minimal movement as is consistent with sleep...the frequency of measurements of the patient chest incline can be reduced, such as every 15 minutes, in order to conserve battery life, enhance sensor longevity, etc." and is silent as to a frequency "longer than every 15 minutes" as is recited in claim 21. Bennet-Guerrero at Column 6 lines 53-59 (emphasis added). Further, the Examiner has alleged that Bennett-Guerrero "Column 26, lines 16-19 describes that the frequency can vary and be any beneficial/useful frequency." Office Action at page 13. However, the Examiner has failed to

provide any evidence in the cited art or in the general knowledge of one of skill in the art that would inform one of skill in the art that a beneficial/useful frequency would be "longer than every 15 minutes" as is recited in claim 21, let alone any explanation of how Bennett-Guerrero, which is directed to "the frequency of measurements of the patient chest incline," would provide any guidance as to what a beneficial/useful frequency is for SEM measurements for "a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers" as is recited in claim 21. See Bennett-Guerrero at Column 6, lines 53-59. Indeed, Applicant submits that one of skill in the art reading Bennet-Guerrero would understand that Bennet-Guerrero recites a longest frequency of 15 minutes, and a preferred frequency of every 1 minute. Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that Bennet-Guerrero is completely silent as to "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements", let alone "making a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, wherein the pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K is longer than every 15 minutes." as is recited in amended claim 21 (emphasis added).

For at least the above reasons, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the amended claim 21 is nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennet-Guerrero.
(b) A person of ordinary skill in the art combining the cited references would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter with a reasonable expectation of success

Notwithstanding that Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest all the elements of amended claim 21, the Examiner alleges that there is motivation to combine Berggren with Lachenbruch and Geleijnse because "Lachenbruch et al. and Geleijnse et al. teaches of obtaining measurements values in a broad manner thus one can replace the broadness with the specificity of determining a delta between sensors in order to obtain predictable results of captured patient data from sensors... Lachenbruch et al. describes using 'other values' in paragraph [00037] therefore... allows for a more specific

determination of measurement values." Office Action at 12. The Examiner also alleges that the motivation to combine Bennet-Guerrero with Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Bergen is that the combination is "beneficial for various reasons such as to enhance, improve, or even optimize battery life." Office Action at 13. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
To establish aprimafacie case of obviousness, there must be some suggestion or

motivation, either in the references themselves or in the knowledge generally available to one of skill in the art, to modify the reference or to combine reference teachings. See M.P.E.P §2143.01. There must also be a reasonable expectation of success. See M.P.E.P §2143.02. Furthermore, if a proposed modification would render the prior art invention being modified unsatisfactory for its intended purpose then there is no suggestion or motivation to make the proposed modification. See M.P.E.P. §2143.01(V)
i) One of ordinary skill in the art combining Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Berggren would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter of amended claim 21 with a reasonable expectation of success.
Applicant submits that one of skill in the art reading Lachenbruch and Geleijnse would understand that, at best, only Lachenbruch recites "other values" in paragraph [0037]:
the sensor collects information regarding subepidermal moisture (SEM) levels as a measure of impedance in dermal phase units (DPU), although other values may be
collected depending on the particular embodiment... [f]or example, if the threshold of
150DMU was based on an average SEM for 20 patients within the individuals'
demographic that developed pressure ulcers within one week, the threshold value may be recalculated to include the individual's SEM of 185 DMU, adjusting the threshold value
up or down, depending on other values within the demographic. Lachenbruch at paragraph [0037] (emphasis added).

Applicant submits one of skill in the art reading Lachenbruch would understand that the alleged "other values" in paragraph [0037] are not "measurement values" as alleged by the Examiner but are demographic characteristics to stratify the data. Accordingly, one of skill in

the art would not understand "other values" to refer to values measuring a disease state. Therefore, one of skill in the art would not consider the term "other values" to suggest the interchangeability of a "specific determination of measurement values" as is alleged by the Examiner for the "other values" recited by Lachenbruch in paragraph [0037]. See Office Action at page 12.

Second, even if, arguendo, one were to apply Berggren to the recitation of Lachenbruch, there is no reasonable expectation of success. As discussed in Section A, Berggren recites "Capacitive affinity biosensors can be constructed by immobilizing recognition elements in thin layers on an electrode or between two electrodes and measuring changes in the dielectric properties when an analyte binds." Berggren at 3rd paragraph of Introduction (emphasis added). Applicant respectfully submits that one of skill in the art reading Berggren would understand that the biosensors of Berggren immobilize an analyte and register a change when an analyte binds. The Examiner has provided no rationale for how a biosensor "measuring changes in the dielectric properties when an analyte binds" (Berggren at page 1) as recited in Berggren would be successful in the method of Lachenbruch which one of skill in the art would understand to require "a measure of impedance in dermal phase units (DPU)." See Lachenbruch at paragraph [0037]. Applicant respectfully submits that one of skill in the art would understand that substituting the "changes in the dielectric properties when an analyte binds" of Berggren (see Berggren at page 1) for the "measure of impedance in dermal phase units" required in Lachenbruch would render the method of Lachenbruch inoperable and therefore unsatisfactory for its intended purpose. See Lachenbruch at paragraph [0037]. Indeed, there is no reasonable expectation of success, let alone any suggestion or motivation for the allegedly obvious substitution to arrive at "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements" as is required by amended claim 21. Applicant submits that Geleijnse is silent as to "calculating a delta value by a difference between a maximum SEM value and a minimum SEM value of the plurality of SEM measurements" as is required by amended claim 21.

For at least the above reasons, one of ordinary skill in the art combining Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Berggren would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter of amended claim 21 with a reasonable expectation of success. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the amended claim 21 is nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren.
ii) One of ordinary skill in the art combining Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren and
Bennet-Guerrero would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter of amended claim 21 with a reasonable expectation of success.

First, as stated in section (a) the Examiner has failed to provide any recitation that would inform one of skill in the art that a beneficial/useful frequency would be "longer than every 15 minutes" as is recited in claim 21. Applicant submits that one of skill in the art reading Bennet- Guerrero would understand that Bennet-Guerrero provides a frequency of measurement of an incline angle of a subject's chest and reducing the frequency for beneficial/useful reasons related to measurement of an incline angle of a subject's chest, e.g., to conserve battery life, not "corresponding to level-K" "for a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers" as is recited in claim 21. Accordingly, one of ordinary skill in the art would understand that Bennet-Guerrero's disclosure of reducing measurement frequency (i.e., more frequent than every 15 minutes) is not a basis for predicting success of the claimed method steps of amended claim 21 for at least the reason that there is no suggestion or motivation to identify "a pre-determined frequency" of "a further plurality of SEM measurements" that is "corresponding to" an identified level as is required in amended claim 21. Hence, there would not be a reasonable expectation of success to apply an element of Bennet-Guerrero's protocol in the methods of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Berggren for reducing measurement frequency, much less a modified version of such a protocol to arrive at the method of claim 21, let alone to achieve an alleged comparable result.

Second, the Examiner has not provided any evidence in the art or general knowledge of one of skill in the art to measure a series of values at a frequency "longer than every 15 minutes," let alone a frequency "equal to every 15 minutes." Indeed, Bennet-Guerrero recites a frequency of every one minute for a high risk level. See Bennet-Guerrero at Column 6 lines 9-10. As

previously discussed in Section (a), Bennet-Guerrero recites a lowest frequency of 15 minutes, and the Examiner has failed to provide any evidence in Bennet-Guerrero or elsewhere that would inform one of skill in the art of what a "beneficial/useful" frequency would be for the measurement of SEM values to provide a "continuity of care for a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers (PU)" as is recited in claim 21. Office Action at page 13. Rather, Bennet- Guerrero discloses the importance of more frequent measurements to "indicate that the patient is attempting to sit up, stand, and/or leave the hospital bed which could predispose the patient to injury" and "for a patient being enterally fed into the stomach, an indication/alarm may provide an indication as to whether the incline of the upper chest/abdomen is less than 30 degrees...relative to the floor." See Bennet-Guerrero at column 7, lines 7-25. In contrast, Applicant's disclosure addresses a "a continuity of care for a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers (PU)" as is recited in claim 21. Therefore, even assuming arguendo that one of skill in the art would look to Bennet-Guerrero for a frequency of measurements as disclosed in Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, or Berggren, they would not arrive at the method of claim 21 as amended with any expectation of success to provide a "continuity of care for a patient at risk of developing pressure ulcers" as is recited in claim 21 based on the monitoring frequency for a patient at risk of changing incline.

Third, the Examiner has alleged that "Bennett-Guerrero.. .was not used to teach the entire limitation..." Office Action at page 4. However, the Examiner has provided no rationale for how any of the other references teach "making a further plurality of measurements at a pre- determined frequency corresponding to level-K..." as is recited in claim 21. Applicant submits that by the Examiner's own reasoning, Lachenbruch and Geleijnse teach away from doing something as is required in claim 21 "if the delta value does not exceed the threshold" by teaching to do nothing. Specifically, the Examiner states that "Lachenbruch et al. teaches ... do nothing if the delta value does not exceed the threshold" and that "Geleijnse et al. teaches... do nothing by continuing to administer the current PU intervention." Office Action at pages 9 and 11. Applicant submits that "making a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre- determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold"

as recited in claim 21 is doing something based on the calculated delta value. Therefore, Applicant submits that one of skill in the art reading Lachenbruch and Geleijnse would find no suggestion or motivation to identify a monitoring frequency of Bennet-Guerrero to arrive at the frequency recited in amended claim 21, let alone make "a further plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold" as recited in claim 21.

For at least the above reasons, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the amended claim 21 is nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennet-Guerrero.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner

withdraw the rejection of claim 21under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, and further in view of Bennett-Guerrero. As claims 23-26, 29, and 37 depend from and include all elements of claim 21, Applicant submit that these claims are also nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennet- Guerrero for the same reason. Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, and further in view of Bennett-Guerrero.
B. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, and Heaton

The Examiner rejects claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, further in view of Bennett-Guerrero as applied to claim 29, and further in view of US Patent 9,675,289 to Heaton ("Heaton"). See Office Action at p. 18.
Specifically, the Examiner asserts that Heaton provides "querying the database for data for form retrieved delta values." Office Action at page 19. As such, the Examiner concludes that

"[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time the invention as filed would have found it obvious to query the database for data to form retrieved delta values as taught by Heaton in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., Berggen, and Bennett-Guerrero in combination with the motivation(s) of being a way to store and retrieve information from a database." Office Action at page 19. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claims 29, 31, 32, 34 and 39 are dependent from claim 21, and incorporates the features of claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, Bennett-Guerrero, and Heaton does not remedy the deficiencies of these references as discussed in Section A above, claims 31, 32, 34 and 39 are also nonobvious.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner

withdraw the rejection of claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, and further in view of Bennett-Guerrero as previously applied to claim 29, and further in view of Heaton.
C. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, and Miller

The Examiner rejects claim 33 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, and further in view of Bennett-Guerrero as applied to claim 29, and further in view of US Publication 2008/0015894 to Miller et al. ("Miller"). See Office Action at p. 21. Specifically, the Examiner asserts that Miller provides "creating an additional record, wherein the data element comprises one or more of a nutritional information, an implemented intervention, a risk assessment, a visual skin assessment, a care plan, a doctor's note, an event, a vital sign, a body weight, and a lab result..." Office Action at page 22. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time of the invention was filed would have found it obvious to 1) create an additional data record, wherein the data element comprises one or more of a nutritional information, an implemented

intervention, a risk assessment, a visual skin assessment, a care plan, a doctor's note, an event, a vital sign, a body weight, and a lab result and 2) report the additional data record to the database." Office Action at page 22. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claims 29 and 33 are dependent from claim 21, and incorporate the features of claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, Bennet- Guerrero, and Miller does not remedy the deficiencies of these references as discussed in Section A above, claim 33 is also nonobvious.

For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 33 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennett-Guerrero as previously applied to claim 29, and further in view of Miller.
D. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, Heaton, and Rothman
The Examiner rejects claims 35 and 36 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, further in view of Bennett-Guerrero, further in view of Heaton as applied to claim 32, and further in view of US Patent 8,355,925 to Rothman et al. ("Rothman"). See Office Action at p. 23. Specifically, the Examiner asserts that Rothman provides "the step of analyzing the retrieved values to determine one or more of a slope, an acceleration, a curve shape and associated characteristics, and a time- to-time intercept of a selected threshold value." Office Action at page 24. Thus, the Examiner concludes "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time of the invention as filed would have found it obvious to have the step of analyzing the retrieved values to determine one or more of a slope, an acceleration, a curve shape and associated characteristics, and a time-to-intercept of a selected threshold value...with the motivation(s) of alerting a user if a patient is getting better or worse at an accelerating rate." Id. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claims 32, 35, and 36 are dependent directly or indirectly from claim 21, and incorporates the features of amended claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, Bennet-Guerrero, and Rothman does not remedy the deficiencies of these references as discussed in Section A above, claims 35 and 36 are also nonobvious.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner

withdraw the rejection of claims 35 and 36 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett-Guerrero, and Heaton as previously applied to claim 32, and further in view of Rothman.
E. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, and Brem
The Examiner rejects claims 40 and 43 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, further in view of Bennett-Guerrero as applied to claim 21, and further in view of "Protocol for the successful treatment of pressure ulcers" (Brem et al., The American Journal of Surgery, 188 (Suppl. to July 2004):9S-17S (2004)) ("Brem"). See Office Action at p. 25. Specifically, the Examiner asserts that Brem provides "wherein the level-0 PU intervention further comprises an intervention selected from the group consisting of providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning every 24 hours, and a combination thereof." Office Action at page 25. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute an intervention selected the group consisting of providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning every 24 hours, and a combination thereof...because they are types of treatment options, making results predictable." Office Action at page 26. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claims 40 and 43 are dependent directly or indirectly from claim 21, and incorporates the features of amended claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero as discussed in Section A above, claims 40 and 43 are also nonobvious.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner

withdraw the rejection of claims 40 and 43 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennett-Guerrero as previously applied to claim 21, and further in view of Brem.
F. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, and Lamont

The Examiner rejects claim 41 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, further in view of Bennett- Guerrero as applied to claim 21, and further in view of US Patent 5,367,789 to Lamont ("Lamont"). See Office Action at p. 27. Specifically, the Examiner asserts that Lamont provides "a level-1 PU intervention of providing a heel boot to the patient." Office Action at page 27. Thus, the Examiner concludes that "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-1 PU intervention of providing a heel boot to the patient...because they are types of treatment options, making results predictable." Office Action at pages 27-28. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claim 41 is dependent from amended claim 21, and incorporates the features of amended claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero, and Lamont does not remedy the deficiencies of these references as discussed in Section A above, claim 41 is also nonobvious.

For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claim 41 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennett-Guerrero as applied to claim 21, and further in view of Lamont.
G. Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, Bennett- Guerrero, and DuDonis

The Examiner rejects claim 42 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren, further in view of Bennett- Guerrero as applied to claim 21, and further in view of US Patent 6,634,045 to DuDonis et al. ("DuDonis"). See Office Action at p. 28. Specifically, the Examiner asserts that DuDonis provides "a level-2 PU intervention of changing the patient's support surface." Office Action at page 28. Thus, the Examiner concludes "it would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to substitute a level-2 PU intervention of changing the patient's support surface as taught by DuDonis et al. for a treatment level as disclosed by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., Berggren, and Bennett-Guerrero in combination." Office Action at page 29. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
